title: Dissipative properties of isoscalar collective excitations in heavy nuclei
summary: The dissipative properties of isoscalar collective motion in heavy nuclei are studied within a kinetic model of collective excitations in finite Fermi systems with a free moving surface. The model includes both the one-body damping produced by the interaction of nucleons with the dynamic surface of nucleus and the Landau damping mechanism. In this paper, we study the damping and dissipative properties of the isoscalar dipole collective modes and the isoscalar vortex octupole mode, which are formed due to dynamic effects of the nuclear surface. To study the damping mechanism of the considered collective modes, a multipole strength function is used in various approximations. It is shown that the damping of the considered isoscalar collective modes is due to a one-body damping mechanism. An analytical expression for the dissipation coefficient at finite frequency for the collective variable describing multipole oscillations of nuclear surface is obtained. It was found that the dissipation coefficient in the energy region of the considered isoscalar collective modes does not exceed the wall formula friction coefficient derived in the one-body dissipation theory. This result confirms the understanding of friction in the wall formula as a macroscopic limit of the one-body nuclear dissipation.

title: Role of the scission-line structure in the formation of the fragment-mass distribution in $^{180}$Hg fission
summary: The fission of $^{180}\mathrm{Hg}$ is investigated by studying the stochastic evolution on the potential energy surface calculated within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov (MDC-RHB) model. The MDC-RHB model provides the zero-temperature potential-energy surface in the $(β_{20},β_{30})$ plane and self-consistent density distributions, from which scission configurations are identified using a geometrical neck criterion. The evolution toward scission is described by a master equation on the same deformation mesh, with transition rates determined by deformation-dependent microscopic level densities. The level densities are obtained in a finite-temperature BCS treatment using the MDC-RHB single-particle spectra and zero-temperature pairing gaps as input. The effective barrier-top region is found to lie close to the scission line, making the detailed energetic structure of the scission boundary particularly important for the fragment distribution. The potential-energy landscape and scission-line structure strongly favor reflection-asymmetric configurations with pronounced prefragment deformations and lead to fragment-mass distributions centered close to the experimentally observed $A_{\mathrm L}/A_{\mathrm H}\simeq80/100$ division. An additional constrained $β_{40}$ analysis indicates that fluctuations beyond the $(β_{20},β_{30})$ collective space can generate an additional spread of the fragment masses. With increasing excitation energy over the range $E^*=34.0$--$65.5$ MeV, the symmetric component is enhanced, while the asymmetric fission mode remains dominant.

title: Spin Asymmetries for Twisted-Neutron Capture by Polarized $^3$He Nuclei
summary: We provide a theoretical analysis of a nuclear reaction caused by twisted neutrons that carry an additional Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) along the propagation direction. Angular momentum selection rules are derived for the thermal-neutron capture reaction on a spin-polarized $^3$He nucleus. We demonstrate that noticeable novel spin effects due to OAM are limited to the region of the size of de Broglie wavelength around the phase singularity of the beam. Spin asymmetries are predicted for a range of experimental constraints.

title: Probing deformed nuclei: Experimental insights into excited states of $^{152,153,154}$Gd isotopes through fusion-evaporation reactions
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures. Accepted manuscript. Published in Nuclear Physics A 1047 (2024) 122888, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nuclphysa.2024.122888
summary: The rare-earth region has been the focus of various studies aiming at the understanding of nuclear structure and providing information on the details of the reaction mechanism. The Gd isotopes belong to this group of nuclei and despite the available spectroscopic information, several open questions about their structure still exist, such as the inter-band transitions related to shape evolution or branching-ratios in deformed states. In addition, production cross sections of different reactions to Gd isotopes are largely unknown. In this work, we report on an experimental attempt to populate the excited states in the isotopes $^{152,153,154}$Gd by employing the heavy-ion fusion reaction $^{18}$O+$^{138}$Ba $\rightarrow$ $^{156-x}$Gd + $xn$ in the 58-64 MeV energy range (center-of-mass). The experiment was conducted at the 9 MV FV Pelletron Tandem at the Horia Hulubei National Institute for Physics and Nuclear Engineering, employing the ROSPHERE array. Several branching-ratios for energy levels in $^{152,153}$Gd have been measured, offering new and updated values. Furthermore, relative cross sections regarding the fusion-evaporation reactions $^{138}$Ba($^{18}$O, 4n)$^{152}$Gd, $^{138}$Ba($^{18}$O, 3n)$^{153}$Gd, and $^{138}$Ba($^{18}$O, 2n)$^{154}$Gd have been measured and compared with theoretical calculations with PACE4.

title: Elliptic flow of $φ$ and $Ω$ via quark recombination mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: Multi-strange hadrons, such as the $φ$ meson and $Ω$ baryon, serve as unique probes for the properties of the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Using a quark recombination model with the quark phase-space information parameterized in a viscous blastwave, we show that the elliptic flow $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$ can be describled by quark recombination in a wide energy range from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV. We check the scaling properties of $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$ and find the number-of-constituent-quark (NCQ) scaled $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$ are approximately equal. We further present the $v_2$ of strange quarks at hadronization extracted from $φ$ and $Ω$ data. We find the $v_2$ of strange quarks is close to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$ at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7-200 GeV, but significant larger than the latter at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76-5.02 TeV, suggesting that the $v_2$ of strange quarks cannot be simply equated to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $φ$ and $Ω$. Our results demonstrate that the quark recombination mechanism is valid for $φ$ and $Ω$ production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV, indicating the existence of constituent quark degree of freedom at these energies.

title: Precise measurements of the 3H/3He charge form factor ratio and their impact on the 3H-3He charge radius difference
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, submitted to Phys. Rev. C
summary: Nuclear form factor measurements can be used to extract the nuclear charge radius. These can be compared to ab initio nuclear structure calculations, with the difference between 3H and 3He charge radii providing information on the spatial distribution of protons vs neutrons in these nuclei. Extractions of the 3H-3He charge radius difference are limited by the modest amount of data for tritium elastic scattering at low momentum transfer. The experiment made a precise measurement of the 3H/3He form factor ratio at low momentum transfer which is combined with the absolute 3He measurements to provide improved 3H data. This provides an improved determination of the absolute normalization corrections of world data sets, giving improved precision for the low-Q^2 measurements that are most sensitive to the radius. We extract the elastic cross sections and the 3H/3He ratio at Q^2=3.03 fm^{-2} and evaluate the impact of this point on a global fit of previous form factor extractions. We examine both the impact on the normalizations of the other data sets and the fit parameters, including the charge radius and its uncertainty. Our sensitivity study shows that the new precision data points constrain the normalization of previous data sets, reducing the uncertainties by up to 12% and yielding a 4% improvement in the radius. Including projected data based on an approved experiment yields improvements in the normalization factors of up to 20% and a 27% improvement in the 3H RMS charge radius extraction, allowing for an improved extraction of the 3H-3He radius difference from a direct fit to the form factor ratios over a range in Q^2.

title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
comment: 17 pages; comments and feedbacks are welcome
summary: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4π\bmod 1/2π$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.

title: Proton Number Fluctuations in Au+Au and Ag+Ag Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$: A JAM Model Study
summary: Proton number fluctuations in low-energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive to nuclear interactions, baryon-number conservation, and fluctuations of the collision volume, all of which can complicate searches for critical phenomena. We investigate proton-number cumulants and factorial cumulants up to fourth order in Au+Au and Ag+Ag collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=2.4\ \mathrm{GeV}$ using the JAM hadronic transport model in cascade and mean-field modes. We employ the Centrality-Independent Genuine Cumulant Analysis fRamework (CIGAR) to suppress the initial-volume fluctuations and compare its results with those obtained using conventional centrality-bin-width corrections. CIGAR closely reproduces the participant-number-based reference, whereas the multiplicity-based analysis exhibits substantial deviations. In both collision systems, the ratios $C_{2}/C_{1}$, $C_{3}/C_{1}$, and $C_{4}/C_{2}$ generally decrease toward more central collisions and with increasing rapidity acceptance, while the mean field modifies their magnitudes. A simplified treatment of light-nucleus formation through probabilistic proton removal shifts $C_{4}/C_{2}$ toward less negative values. These results establish a hadronic-transport reference without an explicit QCD critical contribution and highlight the importance of controlling centrality fluctuations, acceptance, and light-nucleus formation when interpreting experimental measurements at high baryon density.

title: Symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory
summary: A symmetry-preserving higher-derivative formulation of the non-relativistic baryon chiral effective field theory is introduced. Integral equations for the two-nucleon scattering and the deuteron structure functions are derived and numerical solutions at leading order are obtained.

title: Collective Signatures of Pionic Correlations at High Momentum Transfer
summary: High-momentum-transfer reactions have provided experimental evidence for enhanced pionic correlations in nuclei, yet the microscopic connection between the low-energy pionic response and the delta-hole excitation spectrum remains unresolved. Here we identify hybrid pion-delta collective modes that emerge through the coherent coupling of nucleon-hole and delta-hole excitations. By evaluating the full delta-hole Lindhard function within the random-phase approximation, we find a robust low-energy hybrid pion-delta mode and a higher-energy collective delta-hole mode. The low-energy mode is strongly enhanced as the Landau-Migdal parameter is reduced, exhibiting behavior characteristic of a precursor to pion condensation. We further show that these modes may be probed through high-momentum-transfer charged-pion production reactions. Because the same collective pion-delta function governs both the response and the RPA correlation energy, our results connect experimentally observable collective excitations with microscopic many-body correlations.

title: Isospin violation and the neutron weak magnetic moment
summary: The recent measurement of weak magnetism in neutron beta decay [1] obtained a value that is consistent with the conserved vector current hypothesis requiring the assumption of isospin conservation. The influence of the quark-mass difference and electromagnetic effects that violate this conservation law are examined using non-relativistic constituent quark models and estimated to be of the order of at most 1%.

title: Role of Wigner SU(4) Symmetry in Low-Energy Spin-Isospin Transitions of Three-Valence-Nucleon Systems on LS Closed Cores
summary: We investigate low-energy Fermi (F) and Gamow--Teller (GT) transition strengths in three-valence-nucleon systems from the viewpoint of Wigner SU(4) symmetry. For $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$, shell-model calculations show that the ground states contain a large component of the SU(4) representation whose spin-isospin wave function is fully antisymmetric. By varying the spin--orbit splitting in the shell-model Hamiltonian, we demonstrate clear correlations of the SU(4) overlap with both the GT strength to the ground state and its fraction of the total GT strength. For $^{7}{\rm Li}$--$^{7}{\rm Be}$, shell-model calculations show that the $3/2^-_\mathrm{g.s.}$ and $1/2^-_1$ states both belong predominantly to the same supermultiplet as the $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground states. The observed strong GT transitions to these states are therefore interpreted as transitions within the same SU(4) multiplet, split by the spin-orbit interaction. Thus, Wigner SU(4) symmetry provides a unified interpretation of low-energy GT strength concentrations in three-valence-nucleon systems. In particular, the concentration of both F and GT strengths in the same $^{19}{\rm F}$--$^{19}{\rm Ne}$ ground-state transition is naturally understood as a three-valence-nucleon extension of the SU(4) mechanism underlying the low-energy strong GT peak in $^{18}{\rm O}$--$^{18}{\rm F}$.

title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Supplemental Material (8 pages) included. Code and data: https://github.com/prashantstar123/urca-neutrino-reabsorption
summary: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

title: Low-lying states of $^{115}$Cd modeled as a valence neutron coupled to $^{114}$Cd
summary: $^{114}$Cd has historically been regarded as an ideal quadrupole vibrator due to its near-canonical level spacings, though this interpretation is disputed due to electromagnetic transition data from the two- and three-phonon states. In this paper we investigate whether, with the extension of including the single-phonon octupole state, the model is still useful in describing the coupling of a neutron to a cadmium-114 core to model the lowest- energy cadmium-115 states, as the triplet states have small to no influence in the calculation. The results thus provide supporting evidence for the tentatively-assigned $J^π$ values of the lowest-energy $^{115}$Cd states. A more- rigorous derivation than often used for the vibrational B(Eλ) is used, in conjunction with the $^{115}$Cd structure calculation, to provide a theoretical prediction of the $^{114}$Cd octupole deformation.

title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
summary: The method of projection onto localized states intended for describing reactions and clustering is examined. In particular, the method offers a simple extension of the no-core shell model to continuum- and clusterized bound states. A critical analysis of a previous realization of the method is provided. A way to minimize the number of basis functions required for convergence is given. An easy way to obtain exactly unitary and symmetric $S$ matrix from calculations is pointed out. The method is tested in one- and two-channel $np$ scattering problems with the Daejeon $NN$ interaction. It is shown that excellent convergence can be reached even when only oscillator states with low number of excitation quanta are retained.
